thread.title: Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)’s declining iPhone sales threatens investors before earnings call, suppliers’ outlook

author: Grant Pasek
title: Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)’s declining iPhone sales threatens investors before earnings call, suppliers’ outlook
text:
February 1, 2018 Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)’s declining iPhone sales threatens investors before earnings call, suppliers’ outlook 
Last week, many reports have made optimistic predictions related to the demand for Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)’s iPhone X. Nikkei reported that the company is reducing its iPhone X production by half in this quarter, while The Wall Street Journal reported comparable numbers. 
The company’s first quarter earnings release is expected tomorrow, some of the company’s suppliers are providing a peak for it. As Bloomberg noted that both Broadcom and Qualcomm identified during their own respective earnings announcements that iPhone orders have reduced more than normal during this time of year. 
Qualcomm, which supplies modems for the iPhone, said today during its earnings report that “orders from a large, thin modem customer” have declined higher than normal for this time of the year. However, the company has not mentioned Apple by name but it was broadly interpreted that the customer was Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL). 
Moreover, Broadcom made comparable comments today during its earnings release. The company reported that it anticipates “a greater-than-seasonal drop in wireless” components. This indicates that a company is placing less orders for wireless components than usual at this time of the year, and some believe that the company is Apple. 
Broadcom offers Bluetooth components and wireless network for the iPhone. An analyst at Susquehanna Investment Group, Christopher Rolland, defined Apple in a note on Wednesday as the reason for slowing orders. Neither company has mentioned Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) in its predictions. 
Finally, Qorvo Inc., a smaller supplier that generates radio frequency chips, missed analyst estimates. The company has predicted present quarter sales of as little as $645 million, about $100 million less than analyst forecasts. According to Bloomberg, Qorvo obtains about 40 percent of its business from Apple. 
Apple has noted that it projects revenue between $84B and $87B in the fourth quarter of 2017. The company is projected to hold its quarter 1 earnings call tomorrow, offering a more detailed look at those numbers. The company will also provide guidance for quarter 2 of 2018. About Grant Pasek
